freshness.policy: Change-driven: any newer cited source review invalidates the question snapshot. No calendar-based expiry; re-retrieve and independently review after documentation/taxonomy changes. Fresh is relative to checked-in evidence, not a claim of perpetual correctness.

sources.title: Understand scope for Azure RBAC
sources.shortSummary: Azure RBAC supports management-group, subscription, resource-group and resource scopes. Lower scopes inherit the access assigned above them.

sources.title: Azure built-in roles
sources.shortSummary: The built-in-role table distinguishes read-only Reader, resource-managing Contributor, and Owner with role-assignment permissions. Only these cited role definitions support this batch.

sources.title: Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure
sources.shortSummary: CanNotDelete allows management changes while ReadOnly also blocks updates and management POST operations. The most restrictive inherited lock applies across roles, but management locks do not protect data-plane operations.

sources.title: Azure Policy definitions effect basics
sources.shortSummary: Policy assignments are evaluated independently and restrictions are cumulative across scopes. A child audit assignment does not override an inherited deny.

sources.title: Grant limited access to Azure Storage resources using shared access signatures (SAS)
sources.shortSummary: User delegation SAS uses Microsoft Entra credentials; service and account SAS use account keys. Stored access policies apply to service SAS and provide permission revocation without key regeneration.

sources.title: Azure Storage redundancy
sources.shortSummary: ZRS supplies primary-zone redundancy; GZRS adds asynchronous secondary-region replication. RA-GZRS adds secondary read access without failover, with potential replication lag and no immediate secondary write access.

sources.title: Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management overview
sources.shortSummary: Lifecycle rules combine filters with logical AND and can apply deletion to selected blobs. Deletion honors enabled soft delete, and lifecycle deletion does not remove an already-soft-deleted blob before retention ends.

sources.title: Object replication for block blobs
sources.shortSummary: GA block-blob replication requires source change feed and both-account versioning. Archive blocks replication, rehydration needs a subsequent source data update, and active destination containers reject direct writes. Preview index-tag replication is not tested.

sources.title: Set up staging environments in Azure App Service
sources.shortSummary: Supported App Service tiers provide slots for content swaps and rollback. Connection strings can be marked slot-specific; target settings may be applied to source instances during swap warm-up.

sources.title: Set scaling rules in Azure Container Apps
sources.shortSummary: Container Apps limits and event rules jointly control replicas. A no-ingress app without custom rules can be stranded at zero; Service Bus rules support managed identity, configured through CLI or ARM rather than the portal, with single mode for non-HTTP event scaling.

sources.title: Use the Azure portal to enable end-to-end encryption using encryption at host
sources.shortSummary: Encryption at host uses platform-managed keys for temporary disks and the managed disks' selected key type for OS/data caches. Supported VM size and feature enablement prerequisites apply; VMs with Azure Disk Encryption history are restricted.

sources.title: Azure Resource Manager deployment modes
sources.shortSummary: Incremental ARM deployments preserve omitted resources, not omitted properties of included resources. Included resources need their intended final non-default configuration; complete mode can delete omitted resources and is not recommended for new deletion workflows.

sources.title: Azure network security groups overview
sources.shortSummary: NSGs process lower numeric priorities first and stop at the first match. Stateful flow records preserve established connections after rule changes while new connections use the updated rules.

sources.title: Azure virtual network traffic routing
sources.shortSummary: Azure chooses the longest matching route prefix before applying route-source precedence to equal prefixes. Preferred VNet, peering and service-endpoint system routes have documented exceptions excluded from the tested scenario.

sources.title: Alert processing rules
sources.shortSummary: Alert processing rules can suppress action groups for scoped, scheduled maintenance while fired alerts remain visible. Scope and propagation must be considered; Service Health alerts are outside this feature.

sources.title: Run a test failover (disaster recovery drill) to Azure
sources.shortSummary: Site Recovery test failover supports isolated drills. Latest processed avoids processing additional received data, whereas Latest processes received data to favor recovery-point freshness; application-consistent choices serve distinct consistency requirements.

sources.title: Tutorial: Enable users to unlock their account or reset passwords using Microsoft Entra self-service password reset
sources.shortSummary: SSPR can be enabled for None, Selected or All. The Microsoft Entra admin center selects one group, and nested groups can define a pilot population; registration is separate from enablement.

sources.title: Remediate non-compliant resources with Azure Policy
sources.shortSummary: Policy remediation uses the assignment's managed identity rather than the initiating administrator. Editing roleDefinitionIds does not update identity permissions automatically, even for assignments originally created in the portal.

sources.title: What is Azure role-based access control (Azure RBAC)?
sources.shortSummary: Azure RBAC combines all applicable direct and group-derived role assignments. Adding Reader at a narrower scope does not subtract inherited Contributor permissions; deny assignments remain a separate evaluation step.

sources.title: Soft delete for blobs
sources.shortSummary: Without HNS or versioning, overwriting a protected blob creates a soft-deleted snapshot. Undelete restores snapshots and a copy promotes the chosen snapshot to current content; retention and versioning settings change recovery semantics.

sources.title: Define the order for deploying resources in ARM templates
sources.shortSummary: ARM dependsOn arrays accept resource names or IDs to establish prerequisite order. Independent resources deploy in parallel; the dependent resource contains the array.

sources.title: Change the size of a virtual machine
sources.shortSummary: A desired VM size unavailable on the current host cluster can require deallocation. Resizing a running VM restarts it, deallocation releases dynamic addresses, and persistent OS/data disks are retained.

sources.title: Run containerized tasks with restart policies
sources.shortSummary: ACI OnFailure explicitly retries nonzero process exits without repeating successful completion. Always repeats completed processes; current Never documentation allows some platform restarts after nonzero exits.

sources.title: Use private endpoints for Azure App Service apps
sources.shortSummary: App Service private endpoints provide inbound Private Link access, not outbound app connectivity. Public access must be explicitly disabled for isolation, private DNS must be configured, and the private endpoint subnet must differ from the integration subnet.

sources.title: Integrate your app with an Azure virtual network
sources.shortSummary: App Service VNet integration provides outbound access to private network resources on supported dedicated tiers. It does not provide private inbound app access and uses an appropriately sized dedicated subnet.

sources.title: What is a virtual network link?
sources.shortSummary: A private DNS zone link without autoregistration permits linked VMs to resolve zone records without automatically adding their own records. Only one link is allowed for a particular virtual-network/zone pair.

sources.title: Azure Load Balancer health probes
sources.shortSummary: Standard Load Balancer probes determine backend eligibility for new connections. IPv4 probes originate from 168.63.129.16 and must pass both NSG rules and the guest firewall to reach the configured listener.

sources.title: Diagnostic settings in Azure Monitor
sources.shortSummary: Resource logs need diagnostic settings. A setting can route to multiple destination types but at most one destination of each type; two Log Analytics workspaces therefore require separate settings.

sources.title: Soft delete for virtual machines
sources.shortSummary: For a soft-deleted Azure VM backup, first use Undelete to recover the retained restore points. The item returns to stopped protection with retained data, permitting Restore VM or a later Resume backup; a fresh backup is not a prerequisite.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Independent reread of scope-overview (Reader on the RG scope inherits to current and future resources; sibling RGs excluded) and built-in-roles (Reader is read-only management) confirms option b is the only choice matching both scope and least privilege; sibling RGs excluded.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Scope-overview parent-child inheritance and built-in Reader permissions independently reread.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Rechecked RBAC overview Multiple role assignments section: sum of Contributor + Reader = Contributor for the scope; Reader assignment has no impact. Groups transitive line supports group-derived Contributor. Additive model contradicts every distractor.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The Multiple role assignments section explicitly states the additive-sum behavior against this scenario.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Verified against effect-basics Layering policy definitions: assignments are independently evaluated and the layered net effect is cumulative most restrictive, mirroring the article example with deny at subscription and audit at RG. centralus violates the subscription deny.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Effect-basics example directly maps to the scenario with matching allowed-region prefixes and effects.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Remediate-resources How remediation access control works separates evaluation identity (caller) from remediation identity (assignment managed identity). Configure the managed identity note explicitly states later roleDefinitionIds edits require manual permission grants, even in the portal. Managed-identity location does not affect Policy operation.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The remediation article isolates the exact edited-roleDefinitionIds warning that matches the failure symptom.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Storage-sas overview table shows user delegation SAS authorized via Microsoft Entra ID while service and account SAS are signed with Shared Key. The user delegation key requires the generateUserDelegationKey action, satisfying the delegation-permission precondition.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Table Type of SAS/authorization plus signing-key discussion directly answer the account-key-free requirement.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Storage-sas identifies the service SAS with stored access policy variant that inherits constraints from a server-side policy and can be updated or revoked without key rotation. The article also states account SAS and user delegation SAS must be ad hoc and cannot use stored access policies.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Storage-sas ad hoc vs stored access policy section and note isolate the revocation control asked for.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Storage-redundancy ZRS section confirms primary-zone read/write tolerance; GZRS builds on ZRS in the primary region and asynchronously replicates to a paired secondary; RA-GZRS enables secondary reads without failover. RA-GRS uses LRS in the primary region and does not tolerate zone loss.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Multiple named subsections separately substantiate the primary-zone, secondary-read and asynchronous-lag constraints.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Object-replication Blob tiering explicitly states rehydrating an archived blob does not trigger replication and that replication resumes only when the blob data is updated again after rehydration. Replication rules disallow direct writes to the destination container and versioning cannot be disabled while a replication policy exists.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Blob tiering, Replication rules and Blob versioning subsections independently support the correct action and each rejection.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Lifecycle overview Filters row states multiple filters are combined with a logical AND, so only the double-matching blob is selected. Known issues and limitations state the delete action places matching blobs into soft-deleted state when soft delete is enabled, rather than permanently deleting.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Filters AND semantics and soft-delete integration are both stated in the same lifecycle article.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Resource-dependency article and its network-interface example show dependsOn as an array of resource names or IDs that runs on the dependent resource. Independent resources deploy in parallel. The fragment matches the documented resourceId-style expression on the dependent resource.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The article example directly matches the shown resourceId expression pattern on a networkInterface resource.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Encryption-at-host portal article introductory paragraph states temporary disks and ephemeral OS disks are encrypted with platform-managed keys and OS and data disk caches follow the disk key type (CMK when the disk is CMK). Restrictions list VMs with Azure Disk Encryption history and require deallocate/reallocate.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Introductory statement in the portal article directly maps to the temp-vs-cache key attribution asked in the scenario.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Resize-vm article states deallocation may be required when the desired size is unavailable on the current hardware cluster, resizing a running VM restarts it, and deallocation releases dynamic IP addresses while retaining OS and data disks.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Introductory notes and warnings on resize-vm articulate cluster availability, restart and dynamic-IP release in one place.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Container-restart-policy article defines OnFailure as restart only on nonzero exit and containers are run at least once, Always as restart even after zero exit (default) and Never as no restart on zero exit while noting the platform may still restart on nonzero exits.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The restart-policy table plus Restart behavior with nonzero exit codes section make each option unambiguous.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Scale-app article warns that with ingress disabled and no rule or minReplicas the app scales to zero with no way to start; recommends a custom rule; requires single revision mode for non-HTTP event scale rules; states Service Bus rules support managed identity but the portal does not support managed identity authentication so CLI or ARM must be used.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The zero-ingress note, single-revision requirement, managed-identity support and portal limitation are all in scale-app.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Network-security-groups-overview Priority row states rules run in ascending numeric order and processing stops on the first match; conflict is only rejected for identical priority and direction. Priority 220 fires first and denies.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Priority row of the rule properties table directly encodes the answer and rejects the distractor claims.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Network-security-groups-overview Security rules paragraph explicitly walks through an SSH session remaining connected after removing its allow rule while new SSH connections are blocked. NSGs are stateful via flow records.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The article uses the exact SSH example, aligning line-for-line with the scenario.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Virtual-networks-udr-overview How Azure selects routes section states longest prefix match is applied first, then route source order (user-defined, BGP, system) breaks equal-prefix ties. Preferred exceptions and service-endpoint routes are excluded by the scenario.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The two-step selection algorithm and its exceptions are stated in the same article the source cites.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Private-dns-virtual-network-links article defines a resolution virtual network as one linked without autoregistration whose VMs can query zone records but do not register their own, and explicitly permits only one link between a private DNS zone and a virtual network.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: Registration virtual network and Resolution virtual network sections plus Other considerations directly encode the choice.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Alerts-processing-rules Suppress notifications during planned maintenance section recommends a scoped, scheduled processing rule that removes action groups from fired alerts, leaving the alerts visible; it also warns that disabling alert rules stops the alerts from firing.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The maintenance suppression use case is the exact scenario the article walks through, with tradeoffs enumerated.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Diagnostic-settings article Requirements bullet states a single diagnostic setting can define no more than one of each destination type and multiple destinations of the same type require multiple settings, and each resource can have up to five settings. Diagnostic settings are what select and route resource logs.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The per-type destination limit and per-resource setting cap are stated in a single Requirements bullet.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Soft-delete-virtual-machines walkthrough explicitly says the soft-deleted VM item must first be Undeleted; that returns the item to Stop protection with retain data with all restore points available, from which Restore VM or later Resume backup can be initiated. No fresh backup is required.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The step-by-step portal procedure literally names the Undelete-first sequence and the Stop-with-retain-data end state.

reviewQueue.verificationNotes: Site-recovery-test-failover-to-azure Recovery Point section states Latest processed fails over to the most recent processed recovery point without processing additional data, giving low RTO, while Latest processes received data before failover and app-consistent choices target consistency requirements.
reviewQueue.confidenceReason: The recovery-point bullet list distinguishes latest processed from latest and both app-consistent variants.
